exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 120 postnatal women admitted to the Department of Obstetrics & Gynecology, Government Medical College, Churu, divided into vaginal delivery (n=60) and cesarean section (n=60) groups.
finding: Women who underwent vaginal delivery experienced significantly faster postpartum recovery and fewer complications across multiple parameters compared to those who had a cesarean section.
mod_finding: Mode of birth significantly influenced postpartum recovery outcomes, with vaginal delivery leading to lower pain, earlier ambulation, shorter hospital stay, and fewer complications and breastfeeding difficulties than cesarean section.
